skill.name: cc-skill-continuous-learning
skill.description: Adds a Claude Code Stop hook that flags longer sessions for reusable development patterns.
skill.summary: Flags longer Claude Code sessions for reusable learning.
skill.author: affaan-m

security_audit.summary: The skill is a small Claude Code Stop-hook script, not a network exfiltration tool. The main risks are automatic shell execution, local transcript-derived learning, and persistence under a hidden Claude skills directory. Comment-only hidden path matches were dismissed, while runtime home-directory and hook risks remain confirmed.

remediation.suggestion: Default to a project-local dry-run path, then ask before creating or saving learned skills under ~/.claude.

remediation.issue: Session-derived content may include sensitive details
remediation.suggestion: Show proposed learned content for manual approval and redact secrets, customer names, and project identifiers before saving.

remediation.issue: Hook execution is easy to enable globally
remediation.suggestion: Document that the Stop hook runs after sessions and require explicit per-user setup rather than automatic installation.

remediation.issue: Shell script relies on local tools and configurable paths
remediation.suggestion: Check for jq and grep, validate learned_skills_path, and reject unexpected absolute or world-writable destinations.

semantic_findings.title: Session Transcript Learning Can Persist Sensitive Context
semantic_findings.description: The hook reads the Claude transcript path, counts user messages, and asks Claude Code to evaluate long sessions for reusable patterns saved to the learned-skills path. This can persist project-specific or sensitive lessons across future sessions if users enable it without review.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 42-50 use the Claude transcript path and count messages, while lines 58-60 request evaluation and name the save location. The script does not write transcript contents itself, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Automatic Stop Hook Execution Requires Explicit Consent
semantic_findings.description: The script is designed to run from a Claude Code Stop hook after sessions end. Users need clear opt-in because the hook runs local commands and can create persistent learning state after normal coding sessions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file header and hook example clearly show Stop-hook usage. The hook is manually configured, so this is a consent and transparency risk rather than covert installation.

content.user_title: Review Claude Code Sessions for Learning
content.value_statement: Long coding sessions often contain fixes that are hard to remember. This skill adds a Stop hook that flags reusable patterns for Claude Code review.
actual_capabilities: Provides a Bash Stop hook for Claude Code sessions.
Loads session thresholds and output path from config.json.
Counts user messages in the transcript referenced by CLAUDE_TRANSCRIPT_PATH.
Skips sessions shorter than the configured minimum length.
Creates the configured learned-skills directory before signaling evaluation.
Prints guidance for evaluating reusable session patterns.
limitations: It does not extract or write complete skills by itself.
It requires Bash, jq, grep, and Claude Code hook configuration.
It reads transcript metadata from the local Claude Code environment.
It uses a hidden Claude home directory unless reconfigured.

use_cases.title: Capture debugging lessons
use_cases.description: Review long Claude Code sessions for repeatable fixes and workflow patterns.

use_cases.title: Standardize recurring fixes
use_cases.description: Identify patterns that could become reviewed team guidance or reusable local skills.

use_cases.title: Test learning workflows
use_cases.description: Evaluate how Stop hooks can support memory without adding per-message latency.

prompt_templates.title: Review my last session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the continuous learning hook output to identify one reusable debugging pattern. Show the lesson and why it is worth saving.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a learned skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the session summary and draft a concise learned skill for a repeated workflow. Keep sensitive project details out.

prompt_templates.title: Tune detection settings
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect my continuous learning configuration and suggest safer threshold, pattern, and output path choices for my workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit before enabling
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this hook setup for privacy, persistence, and shell execution risks. Recommend changes before I enable it across projects.

output_examples.input: A long debugging session fixed repeated test setup failures.
output_examples.output: The review identifies a reusable test setup lesson, recommends a short skill name, and asks for approval before saving.

output_examples.input: A short three-message session ended without a reusable pattern.
output_examples.output: The hook reports that the session is too short and does not request learning review.

output_examples.input: A project-specific workaround includes sensitive customer details.
output_examples.output: The review rejects sensitive details, keeps only general workflow guidance, and recommends manual approval.

best_practices: Review generated learning content before saving it to a shared skill directory.
Use a project-local output path when sessions may include private details.
Keep the minimum session length high enough to avoid noisy captures.
anti_patterns: Do not enable the hook globally before reviewing its filesystem behavior.
Do not save raw transcript excerpts as reusable skills.
Do not assume every long session contains a useful pattern.

faq.question: Does this skill automatically create complete skills?
faq.answer: No. The script creates the learned-skills directory and signals Claude Code to review longer sessions.

faq.question: What data does it read?
faq.answer: It reads the transcript path from Claude Code and counts user messages in that transcript.

faq.question: Does it require extra tools?
faq.answer: Yes. The script expects Bash, jq, grep, and Claude Code hook support.

faq.question: Can I change the output location?
faq.answer: Yes. Change learned_skills_path in config.json before enabling the hook.

faq.question: Is it safe for private projects?
faq.answer: Use caution. Review outputs manually and avoid saving sensitive project details.

faq.question: Can Codex use it?
faq.answer: Codex can inspect the files, but the automatic Stop hook is designed for Claude Code.
